As we have previously discussed, we can construct _limits_ of diagrams in a
category $\cat{C}$, see [the post about universal_properties](../universal_properties/index.qmd).

The following are extra special diagrams, because they show up very often:

<div id="diagram-equalizer" class="diagram3d" data-diagram="notebook_equalizer"></div>
<p class="diagram3d-caption"><strong>Figure 1:</strong> An equalizer diagram, which
  is $X \rightrightarrows^f_g Y$.
</p>

<div id="diagram-product" class="diagram3d" data-diagram="notebook_product"></div>
<p class="diagram3d-caption"><strong>Figure 2:</strong> A product diagram, i.e.
  only objects $A_i$ for $i \in I$, where only the identity arrows exist.
</p>

We can now consider the universal cones/i.e. limits over these diagrams, which
will result in:

<div id="diagram-equalizer-cone" class="diagram3d" data-diagram="equalizer_cone"></div>
<p class="diagram3d-caption"><strong>Figure 3:</strong> Two cones $N_1$ and
  $N_2$ over the equalizer diagram from Figure 1</p>

<div id="diagram-product-cone" class="diagram3d" data-diagram="product_cone"></div>
<p class="diagram3d-caption"><strong>Figure 4:</strong> Two cones $N_1$ and
  $N_2$ over the product diagram from Figure 2</p>

:::{.callout-warning}
From here on, I still need to finish this post...
Specifically, we wish to show 

> "Theorem 3.41: In any category, if products and equalizers exist, then limits according to any data type can be constructed" ([Lawvere and Rosebrugh, p. 73](https://assets.cambridge.org/052180/4442/sample/0521804442ws.pdf))
:::
